title: 1955–56 National Hurling League
text:
{{Short description|25th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1955–56 National Hurling League |image = |dates =16 October 1955 – 5 August 1956 |teams =18 |team1 = Wexford |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = 1st |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |two = Antrim |previous = [[1954–55 National Hurling League|1954–55]] |next = [[1956–57 National Hurling League|1956–57]] }} The '''1955–56 National Hurling League''' was the 25th season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==New structure== As a result of a lack of interest from defeated first-round hurling teams in recent years, the [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]]'s [[Structure of the Gaelic Athletic Association|Central Council]] introduced a new system of relegation and promotion for the 1955-56 league. Division 1 was confined to ten teams comprising two groups of five. The bottom-placed team in each group would play off to decide which of the two teams would be relegated. Division 2 was made up of eight teams comprising two groups of four. The first-placed teams in each group contested the final with the winners being promoted. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] | image = 1955–56 National Hurling League final prog.JPG | image_size = 250 |season=1955-56 |winners=[[Wexford GAA|Wexford]]
1st National League title

On 6 May 1956, [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] won the title after a 5–9 to 2–14 win over Tipperary in the final. 1st Division 2 title |relegated= |continentalcup1= |continentalcup1 qualifiers= |continentalcup2= |continentalcup2 qualifiers= |league topscorer= |best goalkeeper= |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1954–55 National Hurling League|1954–55]] |nextseason=[[1956–57 National Hurling League|1956–57]] |updated=22 March 2017 }} In a new departure the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] introduced a second division for the 'second tier' hurling teams. Division 2 featured eight teams divided into two groups - 2A and 2B. The first group featured [[Down GAA|Down]], [[Meath GAA|Meath]], [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] and [[Wicklow GAA|Wicklow]]. The second group featured [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]], [[Roscommon GAA|Roscommon]], [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] and [[Laois GAA|Laois]]. Antrim finished top of group 2A and were crowned champions after defeating group 2B winners Kerry in the final.
